manual.description: This manual documents behavior, implementation, and rationale together. Search by a concept, tag, or evidence target.

sections.title: Foundations
sections.description: Start with the product contract and the architectural boundary that supports it.

entries.title: Local notebooks
entries.summary: Notes remain usable without a network connection.
entries.what: Creates, edits, and searches notebooks on the current device. Changes are available immediately and survive an application restart.

how.lead: The write path crosses three explicit boundaries:
points: The editor emits an immutable note revision.
The repository validates and writes the revision in one local transaction.
A background worker later sends unsynchronized revisions to the remote API.

entries.why: Local-first writes keep the editing path independent from latency and availability. The trade-off is an explicit conflict policy during synchronization.

entries.title: Synchronization conflicts
entries.summary: Concurrent revisions are retained until they can be reconciled.
what: Detects when two devices edit the same base revision.
Preserves both versions and asks the user to choose or merge them.
how: The server compares each revision's parent identifier with its current head.
A mismatch creates sibling heads instead of overwriting either revision.
The client renders the siblings in the conflict resolver.
entries.why: Silent last-write-wins behavior can destroy work. Retaining both heads makes the inconsistency visible and recoverable, at the cost of occasional user intervention.
